title: Steal a Brainrot
genre: Roblox idle tycoon / collect-and-steal (buy meme characters off a conveyor, they generate income in your base, steal others' characters, lock your base)
release_date: 2025-05-16 (Roblox) [CONFIRMED – Roblox experience creation date via Rolimons; English Wikipedia also 2025-05-16; Simple Wikipedia says 2025-05-15]
window_note: in window (launched May 2025; record peak Sept–Oct 2025; still a top-tier Roblox game in Sept/Oct 2026)
developer: SpyderSammy ('Sammy', lead developer; Roblox group 'BRAZILIAN SPYDER' / Spyder Games) – a Spanish-language report also names co-creator 'do_small'; owned/operated by DoBig Studios (Do Big Studios, Florida; founder/CEO John Cannata per Crunchbase).
team_size: Original creators: ~2 (SpyderSammy and do_small) [ESTIMATE – secondary Spanish-language report (Tecnobits), not confirmed by the devs]. Do Big Studios: 18 employees or '21–50' [ESTIMATE – automated company-data sites (Prospeo/Crunchbase-type), contradictory]. Headcount working on the game: no data (no official figure found in 6 searches).
country: Developer group 'BRAZILIAN SPYDER' suggests Brazil (not confirmed); Do Big Studios: USA (Florida).
developer_background: Sammy is the founder and leading developer of the BRAZILIAN SPYDER Roblox group (a fan wiki claims ~22M group members – unverified). Do Big Studios (founded 2020 per Crunchbase – date unverified) runs an 'acquire fast-growing Roblox games and scale/monetize them' model, criticised for heavy monetization (loot-box-like spins, limited-time events) and for buying projects from young creators; it also holds a minority stake in Grow a Garden and partnered with PUBG Mobile on a 'Brainrot Royale' mode (World of Wonder). Exact acquisition terms for Steal a Brainrot: no data.
publisher: DoBig Studios (owner per Wikipedia) – acquisition date/price not disclosed; dev/publisher split unknown.
platforms_and_store_links: Roblox (PC, Mac, iOS, Android, Xbox, PlayStation, Meta Quest via Roblox client): https://www.roblox.com/games/109983668079237/Steal-a-Brainrot ; Rolimons: https://www.rolimons.com/game/109983668079237 ; RoWatcher: https://rowatcher.com/games/7709344486/steal-a-brainrot
business_model: Free-to-play Roblox experience; Robux developer products (buying rare brainrots/lucky blocks, spins/wheels, boosts, base-lock/defence items, event items) and game passes; Roblox Premium payouts. IP licensing: feature film with Story Kitchen announced (creators as producers) [CONFIRMED – Story Kitchen press release].
units_or_downloads: 73,853,301,844 lifetime visits; 29,498,785 favourites [ESTIMATE – Rolimons snapshot, ~Sep/Oct 2026]. Earlier: 30.1B visits around 2025-10-07 (vs Grow a Garden's 32.2B then) [ESTIMATE – PocketGamer.biz citing tracker data]. Average playtime ≈ one-third of Grow a Garden's [ESTIMATE – PocketGamer.biz, Oct 2025]. Max server size: 8 players (Rolimons).
peak_concurrent_players: 25,836,222 on 2025-10-11 (during the 'Yin Yang' event) [ESTIMATE – Rolimons all-time peak; RoWatcher gives 25.8M]. PocketGamer.biz reported 25.4M on 2025-10-07 (also cites 25.2M) – first game ever above 25M CCU; 24.1M in Sept 2025 when it overtook Grow a Garden's ~22.4M record; ~20M+ in late Aug 2025. Helped Roblox hit a platform record 47.4M CCU in Aug 2025 [CONFIRMED – Roblox platform stat via PocketGamer.biz]. Recent: 30-day peak 1,590,113, 7-day peak 1,290,920, 84,173 online at snapshot [ESTIMATE – Rolimons, ~Sep/Oct 2026]; profitable.app showed 135.8k online on 2026-07-30.
steam_reviews: n/a (Roblox). Roblox rating ≈ 85.2% positive (85.164%) [ESTIMATE – Rolimons snapshot ~Sep/Oct 2026]; raw like/dislike counts: no data.
gross_revenue: Reported/tracker figures: Bloomberg estimated >$64M of real-money purchases since launch [ESTIMATE – Bloomberg, cited by a secondary article (L'Essentiel de l'Éco); exact date not shown, likely ~Aug–Sep 2025]. profitable.app: $574.6M lifetime model, $6.9M last 30 days, $259.4K last 24h (snapshot 2026-07-30) – generic visits-based model, effectively creator-side DevEx value, likely overstated. RoWatcher: ~$1.43M/month (82% confidence, undated). Own estimate of lifetime consumer spend (May 2025–Sep 2026): ~$250M–$500M [ESTIMATE – Bloomberg ≥$64M for May–Aug 2025 + ~$25–50M/month during the Sep–Dec 2025 peak (24–26M CCU) + ~$8–25M/month for Jan–Sep 2026 while it still hit 1–1.6M CCU peaks; heavy monetization by DoBig offsets shorter sessions].
net_revenue: ≈ 25–30% of consumer spend → ~$60M–$150M lifetime to the owners (DoBig Studios + Spyder creators) [ESTIMATE – spec Roblox method: ~70% creator share of Robux, DevEx ≈ $0.0038/Robux]. On Bloomberg's ≥$64M alone → ≥$16–19M net. Split between DoBig and Sammy: no data. Legal costs (lawsuits below) unknown.
production_cost: No disclosed figure. Original build by ~2 hobby devs (opportunity cost only; Brazil/LatAm rate ~$3k/person-month would put a 1–2 month prototype at ≈ $3k–$12k) [ESTIMATE – spec method, assumptions stated]. Live-ops under DoBig: no data on headcount; if ~10–15 people × ~16 months × $3–6k ≈ $0.5–1.4M [ESTIMATE – assumption, not reported]. Hosting paid by Roblox.
development_time: Original development time: no data. Viral ramp: released 2025-05-16 → 20M+ CCU by late Aug 2025 (~3.5 months) → 25M+ by early Oct 2025 (~4.5 months) [ESTIMATE – derived from PocketGamer.biz/Rolimons dates].
why_popular: Rode the spring-2025 'Italian brainrot' meme wave (AI-generated absurd characters such as Tung Tung Tung Sahur, Tralalero Tralala, Bombardiro Crocodilo) that was already huge on TikTok with kids – instant recognition with zero marketing cost. Simple tycoon loop: buy brainrots off a conveyor, they earn cash per second in your base, buy rarer ones (rarity tiers up to 'Secret'/'OG'). The hook is theft: you can run into another player's base, grab their best brainrot and carry it home, while they lock their base for a timer and defend it – small 8-player servers make the social drama (betrayal, revenge, trolling) highly clippable. Frequent admin events, limited-time mutations/events (e.g. 'Yin Yang' Oct 2025) and a staged 'admin war' cross-event with Grow a Garden (2025-08-23). Short sessions (about a third of Grow a Garden's playtime) suit mobile kids.
marketing_channels: TikTok and YouTube Shorts (brainrot meme culture, steal/troll clips), Roblox YouTubers, Roblox algorithmic discovery (top-3 position for months), admin-abuse/events announced on Discord and social, cross-promo with Grow a Garden, operator studio DoBig's live-ops playbook; later IP expansion (film deal with Story Kitchen, PUBG Mobile 'Brainrot Royale' partnership by DoBig).
art_style: Low-poly Roblox bases and conveyor; 3D renditions of the AI-generated 'Italian brainrot' meme characters; loud, saturated UI.
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write all Luau systems (conveyor spawning with weighted rarity, income-per-second ticking, base ownership and lock timers, carry/steal mechanics with server-side validation, DataStore saves, MarketplaceService products, events/mutations); Claude Code via Rojo plus Roblox Assistant handle this in days; meme-style characters can be generated as concept art (Midjourney/Scenario) and turned into low-poly meshes (Meshy/Tripo) or found in the free Creator Store; ElevenLabs can do the voice-line style audio. Roblox handles servers and replication. AI cannot: catch the next meme wave in time (timing was the main driver), design economy and rarity pacing, run near-weekly events, prevent exploiters, or grow a TikTok/YouTube audience. IP risk: meme characters are now asserted by their creators (Tung Tung Tung Sahur was removed Sept–Nov 2025 over a licensing dispute; Mementum Lab vs DoBig lawsuit), so a solo dev should create original characters. Copycats appeared within days (Rolimons lists dozens of 'Steal a ...' clones; Fortnite had 'Steal the Brainrot' by July 2025). Toolset: Roblox Studio + Luau + Rojo + Claude Code, Roblox Assistant, Creator Store, Midjourney/Scenario + Meshy/Tripo, ElevenLabs SFX/voices, Suno music, Roblox Ads/Sponsored Experiences.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 1–2 weeks, ~$50–$300 (Claude Pro/Max $20–$100/mo, optional 3D/image gen $20–$60; Roblox Studio free, no store fee; excludes the developer's own living costs)
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 1.5–3 months, ~$1,500–$8,000 (AI tools $60–$250/mo, freelance character modelling/thumbnail art $300–$2,000, Roblox Ads/Sponsored Experiences test budget $500–$5,000, optional creator promos). Weekly events needed afterwards. Excludes own living costs.

data_conflicts: Peak CCU: 25,836,222 on 2025-10-11 (Rolimons; RoWatcher 25.8M 'Yin Yang' event) vs 25.4M on 2025-10-07 and 25.2M (PocketGamer.biz, which also dates the 25M+ mark to September in other pieces) – chose Rolimons' 25.84M as the all-time peak and noted PocketGamer's figure as the earlier record report. Release: 2025-05-16 (Rolimons, en.Wikipedia) vs 2025-05-15 (Simple Wikipedia). Developer: Wikipedia names SpyderSammy with DoBig as owner; Tecnobits names two creators (do_small + SpyderSammy). Do Big headcount: 18 vs 21–50 (automated data sites). Revenue: Bloomberg ≥$64M (lifetime-to-date, 2025) vs RoWatcher $1.43M/month vs profitable.app $574.6M lifetime / $6.9M per 30 days (Jul 2026) – the trackers disagree by an order of magnitude; I used my own range and labelled it ESTIMATE. Recent CCU: Rolimons 30-day peak 1.59M (~Sep/Oct 2026) vs RoWatcher article ~215k ('99.2% below peak') vs profitable.app 135.8k on 2026-07-30 – these are different metrics (peak vs point-in-time) and dates. A low-quality source claimed Epic 'licensed' the game into Fortnite; PC Gamer/Kotaku show Fortnite's 'Steal the Brainrot' is a separate creator-made island – I treat it as a copycat.
notes: Legal/IP: (1) Spyder Games sued Thomas Van Der Voort, creator of Fortnite's 'Stealing Brainrots', for copying UI, objects, artwork, level design and animations (~Oct 2025; outcome: no data). (2) The headline character Tung Tung Tung Sahur was voluntarily removed in early Sept 2025 after a licensing dispute with its creator Noxa and brand agency Mementum Lab, and returned in Nov 2025; a Mementum Lab vs DoBig lawsuit over ownership of the character was reported (Wikipedia). Lesson: meme IP is not free to use once it becomes valuable. Fortnite's separate 'Steal the Brainrot' island (July 2025) became one of Fortnite's most popular UEFN games and sold 200-V-Bucks prize-wheel spins after Epic allowed in-island transactions (Jan 2026), followed by an Epic rule change restricting them. Story Kitchen film deal with DoBig Studios and Spyder Games. Lessons for a solo creator: timing a live meme + a simple social 'steal' mechanic beat polish; small 8-player servers concentrate interaction; an operator studio (DoBig) bought in and scaled monetization; the brainrot trend is cooling (RoWatcher), so copying the theme now is late – copy the structure (idle income + raid/defend + rarity chase) with an original, ownable theme.
